govdocs-archive_org-OklahomaCityFalseFla: A single-sheet document headed Oklahoma City: False Flag advances the claim that the 1995 bombing of the federal building in Oklahoma City was a staged occult state terror attack. Its file heading names the Clintons, the ADL, Freemasons, and a new world order among its charges. No evidence supports the claim; courts established the bombing as the work of Timothy McVeigh and accomplices. The sheet is preserved as captured, without endorsement, as a sample of the conspiracy literature the attack produced.
podcast-joerogan-64iS4iT4UNw:
Rogan tries mad honey on air in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, and the transcript keeps his running report. Mad honey comes from bees that feed on certain flowers in the Himalayas, and it carries a natural toxin that can alter the mind and body.

As the effects build, Rogan describes what he feels while his crew watches and jokes. The talk covers how hunters harvest the honey from cliff hives and why people risk the sting of the trip. Part experiment, part comedy, the segment shows the show's willingness to test a strange claim on the host himself.
podcast-tuckercarlson-E7IdLzxzINw:
Tucker Carlson devotes this episode to the climate agenda as he believes its architects would rather it not be understood. His argument is that climate policy serves as a vehicle for control: over energy, food, movement, and national economies, with the planet's health as its public justification.

Carlson walks through the policies and the people behind them, reading their own statements as confessions of intent. His critics call the framing conspiratorial; his audience hears a suppressed obvious truth. The episode is preserved as delivered, a monologue-style brief against climate governance from one of its most effective opponents. Listeners who follow the energy debate will find the strongest popular version of the skeptical case here, and can measure it against the scientific consensus it rejects.
podcast-tuckercarlson-xa6M7n_swNw:
Episode one of Tucker Carlson's series The 9/11 Files opens with what he calls the CIA's secret mission gone wrong. The series promises a fresh look at the intelligence story behind the September 11 attacks. Carlson hosts and narrates the investigation himself.

This opening chapter lays out the agency operation he says set the tragedy in motion. It introduces the men, memos, and missed chances the series will follow. Carlson asks why so much of the record stayed sealed for so long. Questioning and persistent viewers get the first piece of a case built to reopen the file.
